abstract: At the centre of a non-rotating black hole a curvature measure that no change of description alters grows without bound, so the breakdown is real. [[c:singularity.non-removability-invariant-argument]] Both radial light directions swing inward and merge into one at the centre. [[c:singularity.cones-fold]] The obstruction is a direction with no partner, so the repair enlarges the algebra to supply one. [[c:singularity.type-n-only-type-n]] Each step up the resulting tower adds exactly one fermionic mode built from vectors. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]] Inside the hole, Einstein's equations for empty space amount exactly to a marker on the metric staying constant. [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]] Coming back down is the same as averaging each observable with its parity-flipped version. [[c:singularity.descent-parity-average]] For a mode whose mixed state gives both outcomes some probability, the partner making the doubled state pure is the mirror copy of its own algebra. [[c:singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant]] Whatever the starting state, each descended mode of nonzero weight reads as thermal at exactly one temperature. [[c:singularity.descended-form-state-independent]] The entropy gained in coming down measures how distinguishable the state is from its descended version, and is never negative. [[c:singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly]] Two premises, on allowed states and on smoothness at the horizon, put every mode at the same Hawking temperature. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]] The algebra alone cannot choose that value: its symmetries only flip the sign of an inverse temperature. [[c:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic]] At that temperature the Fermi-Dirac filling is the only simple Gaussian state thermal for the boost clock. [[c:hawking.i-state]] Given the s-wave modelling convention, its collective boson modes have exactly the Bose-Einstein occupancy, up to an exponentially small correction on a finite window. [[c:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections]]
introduction: This guide follows a black hole from its centre, where the usual mathematics breaks down, to the radiation it gives off. [[t]] It starts at the singularity, because everything later depends on knowing exactly what has gone wrong there and what kind of repair it calls for. [[t]] Two short sections then describe the enlarged algebra that makes the repair, called the completion: how much room it has for quantum modes, and what Einstein's equations look like inside it. [[t]] With the completion in place, the guide follows the return journey back down to the observables of a single mode, and asks what that step keeps and what it throws away. [[t]] The next section puts a price on the return journey, measured as a gain in entropy. [[t]] The last section shows how the same ingredients produce a temperature, why the algebra alone cannot set its value, and how the resulting state describes the radiation. [[t]] Results that the argument uses without proving are gathered at the end and cited rather than shown. [[t]]
i:singularity: This section looks at the centre of the black hole, shows that the breakdown there is real, and identifies what kind of breakdown it is. [[t]]
t:^>singularity.non-removability-invaria: We begin with a quantity that no change of description can alter. [[t]]
t:singularity.non-removability-invariant: With the breakdown shown to be genuine, we watch what happens to the paths of light on the way in. [[t]]
t:singularity.cones-fold>singularity.typ: Knowing which direction collapses, we can now name the kind of obstruction it is. [[t]]
i:tower: This short section asks how much room for quantum modes the completion provides as it is built up. [[t]]
t:singularity.type-n-only-type-n>tower.w: Since the repair works by enlarging the algebra, the natural next question is how much the enlargement can hold. [[t]]
i:einstein: Here the question is what form Einstein's equations for empty space take once the completion is in place. [[t]]
t:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity>inte: From the algebra of the completion we turn to its geometry. [[t]]
i:descent: Having gone up into the completion, we need a way back down to what a single mode can show us, and this section studies that return step. [[t]]
t:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equatio: With the geometry settled, we look first at the map that comes back down from the completion. [[t]]
t:singularity.descent-parity-average>sin: Because coming down discards information, it is natural to ask where the partner that keeps the larger state pure comes from. [[t]]
t:singularity.purity-output-partner-comm: Turning from the doubled state back to a single mode, we ask what shape its descended state can take. [[t]]
i:entropy: Coming down is not free, and this section measures exactly what it costs. [[t]]
t:singularity.descended-form-state-indep: Knowing what the descent leaves behind, we now put an exact figure on what it removes. [[t]]
i:thermality: The last section turns the descended states into a temperature, and that temperature into radiation. [[t]]
t:singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-desce: With the cost understood, we use the two premises to fix which temperature the descended modes actually have. [[t]]
t:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-: Having found the Hawking value, we ask how much of it the algebra itself determines. [[t]]
t:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-: With that caution in mind, we assemble the thermal state across all the boundary modes together. [[t]]

conclusion: The breakdown at the centre of a non-rotating black hole is a feature of the solution itself, not of how it is written down. [[c:singularity.non-removability-invariant-argument]] It is the kind of obstruction caused by a direction with no partner, so the repair is to enlarge the algebra and supply one. [[c:singularity.type-n-only-type-n]] Coming back down from the enlargement costs exactly an entropy gain, which is never negative and is zero only when there was nothing to discard. [[c:singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly]] Under the two premises every mode comes out at the same Hawking temperature, with no assumption about correlations between modes. [[c:singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii]] The Fermi-Dirac state at that temperature is the only simple Gaussian state that is thermal for the boost clock of the geometry. [[c:hawking.i-state]] Given the s-wave modelling convention, its collective boson modes on the infinite ladder have exactly the Bose-Einstein thermal occupancy. [[c:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections]] What we assume comes down to a short list. [[t]] The first premise, univalence, says that physical states of the boundary modes give zero average to every quantity that changes fermion number by an odd amount. [[c:singularity.p-univalence]] The second, regularity, asks each boundary mode on its own to look thermal for the black hole's time flow, at the temperature for which the imaginary-time version of the spacetime is smooth. [[c:singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus]] The s-wave convention behind the boson reading is a modelling input rather than a derived result. [[c:hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections]] The value of the temperature also has meaning only once the clock's parameter is converted into physical time, and the algebra does not supply that conversion. [[c:singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic]] One consequence faces observation directly: merging black holes should ring exactly as general relativity says, with no echoes, and a single confirmed echo would refute the framework. [[c:scrambling.no-echo-prediction-registered]]
